result.title: Aligning Thoughts with Answers: Probability Rewards to Tame Thinking Drift
result.summary: This paper studies \textbf{thinking--answer consistency} in vision-language models. We focus on Visual Intention Grounding, where a model infers a target object based on a human intention query and predicts a bounding box. We reveal that previous IoU-based reinforcement learning (RL) frameworks suffer from ``thinking drift'', where the model produces a correct bounding box, despite having an incorrect reasoning process pointing to a different target object. Thus, we propose \textbf{Rita} (\textit{ReInforcing Thinking--Answer consistency}) as a novel RL paradigm to tame the drift. Specifically, Rita introduces two reasoning-label-free RL rewards, constructed from the conditional probability of reference answers: a \textbf{thinking reward} and a \textbf{consistency reward}. It also adopts a difficulty-aware \textbf{data filtering} strategy that selects informative easy-to-medium samples for RL using rollout error rate and reward variance. Extensive experiments on EgoIntention and the new RefEgo-Int benchmarks show that Rita performs consistently superior to the supervised finetuning approaches and vanilla RL-finetuned frameworks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究视觉语言模型在视觉意图定位任务中的「思考—答案不一致」问题：模型能给出正确边界框，但推理过程指向了错误目标对象，并据此提出 Rita 强化学习范式，用基于参考答案条件概率构造的 thinking reward 与 consistency reward，配合难度感知的数据筛选来缓解该「thinking drift」。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及 LVR 主线中「答案是否真正使用推理内容、贡献分配与监督」的问题：其诊断的 thinking drift 与 reasoning-label-free 奖励，可供核查 latent 或显式推理状态是否被答案真实利用，以及不一致检测与奖励设计能否迁移到 latent 推理轨迹。
